overview.problemStatement: The database models the platform's access layer but none of its work. User, Organization, Clinic, UserMembership, Invitation, AuditLog, RefreshToken and PasswordResetToken exist, while patients, doctors and appointments - the entities BP-015 to BP-019 depend on - do not. There is no ERD, no clinical seed and no declared index strategy, so the later scheduling features would invent tables, demos would need hand-made data, and the two hot access paths (a doctor's day, a patient's history) would be written against an unindexed table.
overview.proposedSolution: Model the clinical core - Patient, Doctor and Appointment with an AppointmentStatus enum - every row scoped to a Clinic, with the relations and cascade rules the later features need. Add the two indexes those access paths require, (doctorId, startsAt) and (patientId). Ship the change as a forward-only, additive Prisma migration. Add an idempotent seed producing 3 clinics, 10 doctors, 200 patients and 600 appointments of fictional data, and write an ERD that matches the models.
overview.targetAudience: The teams building BP-015 to BP-019 whose plans name these tables and fields; anyone running the demo who needs a realistic dataset without real patient data; CI and reviewers who need migrate deploy to be one repeatable step.
assumptions: Doctors are staff: a Doctor is a clinic-scoped profile row that may link to a User through userId, not a second identity system.
Patients never authenticate in this version; the Patient table has no credentials.
Scheduling semantics belong to BP-018 and BP-019. This feature defines startsAt, endsAt and status but not availability rules, conflict detection or transitions.
No new dependency: the seed ships a small deterministic generator instead of adding a faker package.
Timestamps are stored UTC; clinic-local rendering is BP-013.
The existing 20261028235000_init_tenancy migration is already applied in development and must not be edited.
outOfScope: Availability, working hours, breaks, leave and slot generation (BP-018).
Appointment booking rules, conflict detection and the status state machine (BP-019).
Queue ordering and the Redis sorted set (BP-029/BP-030).
Patient portal, patient authentication and patient-facing APIs.
A production data-import path; the seed is development-only (CON-506).

userStories.title: A schema later features can build on
userStories.want: the clinical entities already modelled and scoped
userStories.benefit: my feature adds behaviour instead of inventing tables

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the Prisma schema, when I read it, then Patient, Doctor and Appointment exist, each carrying clinicId with a foreign key to Clinic, and Appointment relates to both Patient and Doctor.
Given an empty database, when prisma migrate deploy runs, then every migration applies in order without manual intervention and the clinical tables exist.

userStories.title: Append-only migration on a live database
userStories.want: the schema change to be additive
userStories.benefit: an existing database keeps its data when the migration is applied

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a database already holding the tenancy data, when the new migration is applied, then no existing table is dropped or truncated and no existing row is lost.
Given the migrations have been applied, when they are applied again, then Prisma reports no pending migrations and exits 0.

userStories.title: The indexes the access paths need
userStories.want: the two declared indexes to exist
userStories.benefit: a doctor's day and a patient's history are lookups rather than scans

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the migrated schema, when I inspect Appointment's indexes, then one covers (doctorId, startsAt) and one covers (patientId).

userStories.title: A realistic, fictional dataset
userStories.want: one idempotent command to produce believable data
userStories.benefit: I can demo scheduling without real patient information

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an empty database, when the seed runs, then it creates 3 clinics, 10 doctors, 200 patients and 600 appointments.
Given the seed has run once, when it runs again, then the row counts are unchanged and no duplicate rows are created.
Given the seeded rows, when I inspect them, then every patient and doctor uses fictional details and no real personal data is present.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the repository, when I open the ERD, then it documents every clinical model - Patient, Doctor, Appointment - and their relations to Clinic and to each other.

functionalRequirements.text: The schema MUST define Patient, clinic-scoped (clinicId FK to Clinic), with name, date of birth, phone, optional email and optional gender, plus createdAt and updatedAt.
The schema MUST define Doctor, clinic-scoped, with an optional userId link to User, a specialty, an optional licence number, a consultation duration in minutes and an isActive flag.

The schema MUST define Appointment, clinic-scoped, holding patientId, doctorId, startsAt, endsAt, a status of an AppointmentStatus enum, an optional reason and createdAt/updatedAt, with relations to both Patient and Doctor.
The change MUST be delivered as a new Prisma migration that is additive only: it MUST NOT drop or truncate an existing table, and it MUST NOT modify the already-applied init_tenancy migration.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: prisma migrate deploy MUST complete on an empty database in under 60 seconds without manual steps, so CI can run it unattended.
The new migration MUST be forward-only and additive, so it can be applied to a populated database without a backfill.
The seed MUST complete in under 60 seconds and MUST be safe to re-run at any time. (CON-519)
Every clinical table MUST carry clinicId and a foreign key to Clinic, so tenant scoping is a schema guarantee rather than an application convention. (CON-516)

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: A re-run completes the remaining rows without duplicating the ones already written, because each entity upserts on a natural key.

edgeCases.description: Two patients in one clinic share a phone number.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Allowed; the seeding natural key includes the clinic and the person index, not the phone.
Rejected by the seed generator; Prisma cannot express the check, so BP-019 must enforce it on write and the spec records the gap.

edgeCases.description: A Doctor row references a User who is deleted.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: userId is SetNull, so the clinic's doctor record survives the identity being removed.

edgeCases.description: A Clinic is deleted while it has patients.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Deletion is blocked by the foreign key (restrict), so clinical data cannot be orphaned silently.

dependencies.name: Prisma
dependencies.notes: Already present and in use; this feature adds models and one migration.

dependencies.name: PostgreSQL
dependencies.notes: Already required; the migration targets it.

dependencies.name: Deterministic generator (inline)
dependencies.notes: No faker package is added; the seed ships a small seeded PRNG so re-runs produce identical data.

risks.description: A migration that rewrites an existing table locks it and fails on a populated database.
risks.mitigation: Additive-only DDL with no table rewrite; AC-003 proves existing rows survive.

risks.description: The seed duplicates rows on a second run and inflates the demo dataset.
risks.mitigation: Upsert on a natural key per entity, with AC-007 asserting the counts are stable.

risks.description: The indexes exist but a later feature queries differently and never uses them.
risks.mitigation: The two indexes are named in FR-005 and verified by AC-005; BP-015 and BP-019 plans must cite them.

risks.description: Fictional seed data drifts into being treated as real.
risks.mitigation: Emails use @riaya.local and example.org, names come from a fixed fictional list, and CON-506 is restated in the seed header.

risks.description: endsAt > startsAt cannot be expressed in Prisma, so invalid rows become possible later.
risks.mitigation: EC-003 records the gap and assigns enforcement to BP-019 instead of pretending the schema covers it.
